news.title: Chelsea vs Hull: Key statistics and facts
news.body_en: The Blues go into our fourth Premier League match of the season in fourth place in the table, three points behind the two sides with 100 per cent records and one behind Saturday’s opponents Hull City, who have won two and drawn one of their matches. Chelsea meet Hull City for the 50th time in all competitions, needing three more goals to reach 100 against the Tigers, who were the first-ever competitive visitors to Stamford Bridge in 1905, when they were beaten 5-1. The sides last met in February, when Chelsea won 4-0 at the MKM Stadium in the FA Cup fourth round. Pedro Neto got a hat-trick and Estevao Willian scored our other goals. The last time Hull were in the Premier League in 2016/17, both league fixtures ended in 2-0 wins for the Londoners, Diego Costa netting in both. Chelsea have won our past nine matches against Hull City in all competitions and are unbeaten in 17 (15 wins, two draws) since the Tigers’ last victory, 3-0 at Boothferry Park in the old Second Division in October 1988. That remains Hull’s only win against Chelsea in the last 36 meetings over more than a century. Chelsea are unbeaten in all 10 Premier League meetings with Hull, having only faced Portsmouth more often in the competition without losing (14). The Blues are undefeated at Stamford Bridge against the Tigers in 23 matches in all competitions. Hull’s four victories against us have all been at their former grounds Anlaby Road (1906, 1911, 1925) and Boothferry Park (1988). Reggie Watson's dad Ben played for Wigan that day. Reggie was 14 weeks old at the time. Chelsea are aiming to win three straight Premier League games at Stamford Bridge for the first time since the final three home matches of the 2024/25 campaign, and to win our opening two home league games of a season for the first time since 2021/22. Chelsea are the first team in Premier League history to score in the opening five minutes of their first three games of a season - Joao Pedro vs Fulham (31 seconds), Romeo Lavia vs Brighton (3 minutes, 39 seconds) and Morgan Rogers vs Arsenal (1 minute, 17 seconds). Last weekend was the first time Arsenal had conceded within the opening two minutes of a Premier League game for three years. Against Arsenal, Emi Martinez made eight saves, including seven from shots inside the box, and stopped three big chances - the highest totals by any goalkeeper in a Premier League match this season. Cole Palmer has made 78 passes ending in the opposition half in the Premier League, more than any other Blues player this season. No player in the Premier League this season has been fouled more times than Joao Pedro (11). Palmer has 15 goal involvements in his 15 Premier League games for Chelsea against newly promoted sides (nine goals, six assists). Against Arsenal, Danny Welbeck became the first player ever to make a Premier League appearance for each of Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United. Cole Palmer has scored 49 goals in 99 Premier League games for Chelsea. Only two players have reached 50 for the Blues in fewer than 100 games – Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink (84) and Diego Costa (85). Moises Caicedo’s next appearance will his 150th for the club. They are only the third promoted team to keep a clean sheet in each of their first three Premier League games, after Charlton (1998/99) and Huddersfield Town (2017/18). Hull allowed Aston Villa just one shot on target last weekend and had only 26.5 per cent possession. Hull have lost eight of their last nine Premier League games in London (one win), failing to score in all eight defeats. news.title: Training gallery: Rest, recovery and getting ready!
Five key talking points from Sonia Bompastor's pre-Man Utd press conference
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor faced the media at Cobham ahead of our second Women's Super League match of the season against Manchester United on Sunday. Here are the key takeaways from our head coach's press conference... Bompastor confirmed Melvine Malard will not be fit enough to face her former club, while Mayra Ramirez and Manaka Matsukubo remain out. A late decision will be taken on Nathalie Bjorn, who is expected to travel with the squad to the North-West. Both sides go into the game off the back of disappointing results. The Blues were held to a 1-1 draw by Aston Villa at Stamford Bridge despite dominating the contest and creating plenty of good chances. Man United, meanwhile, were beaten 2-1 at London City Lionesses. As well as looking ahead to this weekend's game and how her side will respond, Bompastor reacted to the Ballon d’Or awards, including the news Hannah Hampton could retain her Yashin Trophy. Here is a summary of the best moments from Bompastor’s media conference… ‘She's a big asset, for sure. She's been playing well. My first season, she was unbelievable. We struggled a little bit more as a team last season, and we conceded more goals, but she’s one of the best in the world. I have already said that a lot. ‘The way we want to play, she's a big asset, with the quality she has as a goalkeeper in possession, out of possession. So I'm really happy to have her in my squad.’ ‘I'm pleased with the answer from the players on the pitch. I'm not concerned about how good we are training. I think the intensity, the desire, the mindset is there in terms of working hard, trying hard. We need to reflect and be honest with each other in terms of what we are missing right now, but also not being too hard on ourselves. ‘We need to find the balance between playing beautiful football and having control in most of the games, but also trying to find a way to put the ball in the net and score some goals.’ ‘We need to keep the confidence and keep working hard. I spoke after the Villa game about the mentality, the mindset. It's a huge part of being ruthless in the box. That game could have been easily 3-0 half-time, and we need to have that mentality when we have the opportunities to kill the game after 45 minutes to do that. ‘This week I was coaching the players in the final details: around timings of the runs in the box, being in the right zones, what type of crosses do we want to deliver, what are the connections between the crosser and the players who are making the runs in the box. ‘It’s just for me to reinforce those messages, to coach them on the pitch, and make sure we get them right on the game on the weekend.’ ‘No. My view is more to say it's always a difficult ground to travel to and to play at Man United, with the fans being hostile. They have a really good team. ‘They lost on the weekend, so I think they will come into this game with the desire to win the game. They are playing at home so yeah, it will be a difficult game for us again.’ ‘That's one of the options I have right now. We played LJ a lot in that position last season because we had a lot of injuries there. She helped the team a lot playing that position. ‘When you talk about LJ, she'll bring the creativity on the pitch. She was the one who was able to score the goal on the weekend. She created a lot of opportunities. ‘My job is to make sure she's performing at her best level but also, to find ways for us as a team to be able to create many situations with her and, sometimes, without her. It's difficult to only rely on one player, and we are more predictable if we rely everything on one player. But when she's at her best, I think she's one of the best players in the world.’

news.title: Bompastor issues Melvine Malard injury update plus news on trio
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has confirmed Melvine Malard will not be fit to face her former club Manchester United this weekend. The attacker picked up a knock in training last week, missing the 1-1 draw with Aston Villa that got our WSL season up and running. And Bompastor has confirmed Sunday’s trip to the North-West will come too soon for the French international. ‘Unfortunately she won’t be able to return to Man United and play the game,’ said Bompastor. ‘She’s close to returning, but probably next weekend.’ Mayra Ramirez, Manaka Matsukubo and Nathalie Bjorn also missed our opening league fixture, and Bompastor provided the latest on that trio, with the most positive news regarding the Swedish defender. ‘All of them won’t be available to play this game,’ said Bompastor. ‘Nat Bjorn is starting to train fully with the team so she will be travelling with us. We will see if she has minutes or not.’ Despite their injuries, it was an exciting week for Matsukubo and Malard, both of whom were nominated for the Ballon d’Or award. Bompastor was thrilled about that achievement and can’t wait to welcome them both back to the pitch. ‘It’s a good look on us in terms of the transfer window this summer! I’m proud of them. It’s really good to be nominees in this list. The Ballon d’Or recognisation is huge in the women’s game. ‘We celebrated them for those nominations. Two of them are new signings, for now they are not on the pitch but when they join the team it will be a big help for us.’

news.title: Those Were the Days matchday heritage event to celebrate 60 years of The Shed
news.body_en: Earlier this week, exactly 60 years had passed since a suggestion that would change Stamford Bridge forever. That moment and the impact on Chelsea’s support that followed are being celebrated at a fan-led gathering at this weekend match versus Hull City. It was in September 1966 that a letter was published in the match programme for a home game against Leicester City. A supporter called Clifford Webb penned the note with the idea to refer to the Fulham Road end of Stamford Bridge as The Shed. It also called for more people to join ‘the fanatics’ there in singing and chanting and the rest, as they say, is history. The name was adopted and it has remained in place ever since, even after the stand was rebuilt in the Nineties. To mark the anniversary, the Chelsea Heritage Partnership (a group within the Chelsea Supporters’ Trust which researches, records and shares our history) has worked with supporters old and new, along with some ex-players, to gather their memories of The Shed, both in video and written form. Plenty of these will be displayed at the special pre-match Those Were the Days heritage event in the Tea Bar, which takes place this Saturday, prior to our Premier League fixture, from 1pm. Fans are invited to come along to the event, which is free for all home match ticket holders on the day, where you can: Read about how The Shed was named and the characters involved in the movement Learn how it was transformed throughout the history of Stamford Bridge Hear first-hand recollections of supporters’ experiences of The Shed Watch clips of iconic matches, moments and goals that lit up The Shed See some of the shirts from the Chelsea Museum worn by Shed heroes from the 1960s onwards Chat with the people who were there and get a sense of what the old Shed was like The matchday programme for the Hull game will also include a special feature on The Shed so make sure you pick up a copy on the day.

news.title: Analysis: How devastating Palmer and Rogers helped turn tie around
news.body_en: Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers have started the season in superb form and the duo combined again to great effect on Wednesday night as we roared back from two goals down to beat Leeds United in the Carabao Cup. Palmer and Rogers were two of four fresh faces introduced by Xabi Alonso at half-time – alongside Reece James and Pedro Neto – with the Blues behind and 45 minutes from being eliminated from the competition. The changes didn’t work immediately as the visitors doubled their advantage early in the second period – but then came the fight-back. Palmer swept home a penalty and just 129 seconds later drew us level with a cute strike from the edge of the box. They were two of five shots Palmer had in the second half, with three struck from inside the box and both that hit the target finding the net. They were Chelsea-high or joint-high game figures, along with the five touches in the opposition box Palmer had as he imposed himself on the contest in devastating fashion. Our No10 was ably assisted by his great mate Rogers, who was voted Player of the Match by Blues fans. The official statistics show Rogers registered three assists, but it’s hard to argue he didn’t also set up our fifth goal, scored by Valentin Barco. The only reason Rogers’ dangerous cross that reached the Argentinean at the back post doesn’t count as an assist is because the Leeds goalkeeper Michael Zetterer got the feintest touch on it. Harsh! Rogers created Danny Welbeck’s first of the evening with a delivery from a similar area, while his clever chested assist for Palmer’s second showcased his guile. The prodded pass that found Neto for his goal was a display of bravery as a Leeds defender closed in to challenge. In total, Palmer created two chances and Rogers four, while the duo also led the way for us in terms of passes played in the final third - 16 from Rogers and 12 from Palmer. The nine passes they exchanged between one another was the most of any attacking combination on the pitch. It is already starting to feel like a telepathic understanding. We were ruthlessly efficient in the second half, scoring with each of our six shots on target. The precision of our finishing is highlighted by the fact our xG (expected goals tally) after the break was 2.09 (in contrast to 0.31 before it). In total we had 11 shots in the second 45 minutes and created five big chances. While we had less possession and completed fewer passes in the second half than we did in the first, when we had the ball, we did more with it. We pinned Leeds back, completing 20 more passes in the final third, taking twice as many touches in the opposition box and playing double the number of passes into Leeds’ defensive third. Our attacking intent created a swell of momentum that proved too hot for Leeds to handle and culminated in a thrilling come-back victory that will live long in the memory.

news.title: Rogers vs Leeds Utd 👀
Neto says free-scoring Blues playing with a smile
news.body_en: Pedro Neto believes Chelsea’s six-goal haul against Leeds United was a natural result of the attacking talent the team possesses and the ‘joyful’ way the Blues are playing under Xabi Alonso. A breathless evening of knockout football at Stamford Bridge saw Chelsea fight back from two goals down in the second half to win 6-3 and book our place in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup. Neto more than played his part. He was one of four players brought on by Alonso during the break to help turn things around, and scored our third goal to give us the lead for the first time with a composed finish after Morgan Rogers had beaten the Leeds defence to the ball and played in his team-mate. ‘Morgan did a really good effort, and me, I just thought to put the ball the other way that it was coming, as I thought the goalkeeper was already coming to the other side,’ explained Neto. ‘I think Morgan did the most difficult part, then I just had to put the ball in the goal, to be honest.’ That was just one moment of an incredible 90 minutes of action, with the Portuguese international reflecting on what changed ahead of our second-half fightback. ‘It's a little bit crazy,’ he admitted. ‘I don't like to concede that many goals, but we are working on that. Of course, we like to score six goals, but to concede three is not a thing that we want to do in a lot of games, but we’re happy for the win. ‘I think in the first half they caused a lot of trouble because they are a physical team, they are really intense. At half-time, the manager spoke about that, that we needed fresh legs, fresh mentality, we needed to be more aggressive. ‘We started the second half conceding the second one, but I think it was a really good test for us. We kept calm and then, with the players that we had and the way we played, it was really good. We scored six goals, got through and we’re already looking forward to the next one.’ The 6-3 win was another example of the potent attacking threat the Blues have demonstrated under Alonso’s leadership, with a total of 16 goals scored already across our five fixtures so far in 2026/27. Needless to say, players like Neto are enjoying themselves on the pitch and feeling full of confidence. ‘I promise we will continue to try to score this amount of goals in a game. It will be very good, to be honest,’ Neto added. ‘It's been really joyful. With the guys that we have on the pitch, with the guys that come on in the game, I think the group is in a top mentality. Everyone wants to help, everyone wants to enjoy. ‘I think we learned a little bit from what happened last season. The boss brought a little bit of freshness in that level and, as you can see, everyone is playing with a smile on their face. Even in difficult situations, we think we can turn it around with the quality of the players that we have. ‘The mentality of the club is to win in every competition that we are in. So we want to compete until the last game in the Premier League. We want to go to the final to win the Carabao Cup and in the FA Cup the same. I think this should be the mentality of the team.’

news.title: Alonso: 'We want to be able to win a boring game'
news.body_en: While Xabi Alonso described our Carabao Cup victory over Leeds United as thrilling, the Chelsea manager is aware his side must be ‘able to win a boring game as well’. Five matches into the Spaniard’s tenure and no Blues supporter, be it those watching in the stands or following from home, can argue they have not been entertained. We have found the net on 16 occasions already this season, with the goals largely shared between Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Danny Welbeck. The area of improvement is keeping them out at the other end. Leeds scored three at Stamford Bridge last night but were ultimately outgunned as the Blues advanced into the fourth round following a 6-3 victory. The Chelsea manager has been pleased with the attacking prowess of his side in our opening matches of the campaign, but acknowledges a better balance must be struck as the Blues continue to develop. ‘It’s early days to assess what we will be,’ Alonso said after our win over Leeds. ‘There are things, in terms of the connections of players and the associations, that I see are going to be important. ‘So we need to keep working on the good things and keep on improving other things. We want to have better balance, to be more solid, to be able to win in a boring game as well, if that happens. ‘But it's five games. For sure, we are now through [in the Carabao Cup] and we have two Premier League games before the international break. They are fundamental. ‘We want to finish well before the break and we have two tough games against Hull and Brentford.’ The first of those two fixtures comes on Saturday, as Hull City make the long trip down from Humberside to Stamford Bridge. And Alonso, whose name was repeatedly chanted by the Blues faithful against Leeds, has highlighted the crucial role our supporters will play once more this weekend. ‘We need them,’ he said. 'We need to create this connection, and we need to have a good feeling in this stadium.’

news.title: Cole Palmer: You can see I’m enjoying my football!
news.body_en: It didn’t take long for Cole Palmer to make an impact against Leeds having come off the bench ahead of the restart. Just ten minutes, in fact. Things hadn’t initially gone to plan following Xabi Alonso’s four half-time substitutions, with Leeds doubling their advantage through Brenden Aaronson. Enter Palmer. Our no.10 fired home a pinpoint penalty after Pep Chavarria was felled, and then barely 90 seconds later drew the Blues level at 2-2 with a clever, disguised finish. Fellow sub Pedro Neto completed the turnaround with another precise strike, making it three goals in seven breathless minutes, with the Blues eventually running out 6-3 victors. Palmer revealed what was said by Xabi Alonso in the dressing room at half-time, helping prompt the turnaround. ‘Up the intensity, play a bit more, come more alive because I think the first half was flat,’ said Palmer. ‘Everyone agreed in the changing room, so we stepped up. ‘I probably haven’t seen a half like that for a while. Leeds are a good team, tough game, but we needed to pull through and we did.’ The dramatic outcome continued our impressive start to the campaign. Palmer, meanwhile, has looked back to his best this season, playing with a swagger and making a decisive impact in the final third. He already has four goals, while collectively we have racked up 16 in just five matches. No wonder Palmer is a happy man right now. ‘You can see I’m enjoying my football,’ he said. 'Me and Morgz (Morgan Rogers), Joao (Pedro), all the attacking players, we’re enjoying it. ‘We’ve still got a bit to go. We’re getting results which is the main thing, and now it’s on to Hull on Saturday.’

Xabi Alonso on how belief was key to thrilling victory over Leeds
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso says his Chelsea players' belief and the Stamford Bridge crowd were crucial to the Blues claiming victory in our ‘thrilling’ Carabao Cup third-round tie against Leeds United. The opening period was far from easy for the Blues. With Alonso making nine changes to his starting XI, we struggled to get into a rhythm and fell behind midway through the half when Tarik Muharemovic headed home for Leeds. Alonso introduced Reece James, Pedro Neto, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers at half-time; it was a decisive decision and one that paid off. Yet Leeds did first add to their lead, as Brenden Aaronson fired home two minutes after the restart. Then came the fightback. Palmer converted a penalty and quickly swept home a second to level the contest. Pedro Neto put us ahead with a fine finish, and Danny Welbeck added our fourth. Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave Leeds brief hope, but Valentin Barco's first Chelsea goal and a late Welbeck second extinguished any comeback. ‘It was thrilling and there were different emotions during the game,' reflected Alonso. 'Things were not going the way we wanted in the first half, and I made those decisions, so I take responsibility and take the blame, not the players. ‘In the second half, we showed a great reaction after conceding the second goal. We kept going, and it was very important to believe and get the crowd excited. They helped us a lot.' On his quadruple half-time substitution, Alonso added: '[We asked that] they try to have a good impact in energy, in aggressiveness, in tempo, in duels, because we were struggling in that moment against a very intense Leeds. We did very well. I take context for the first half and I will assess my own decisions. 'Even in the first half, I’m not going to blame the attitude. There were many new things together and they were not working – that is my responsibility. Afterward, once you score, you start believing, looking better and making better decisions. 'So it’s about the mind of the players, the feeling and it was much better in the second half.'

news.title: Highlights: Chelsea 6-3 Leeds Utd
'The fans really helped us in the second half'
'My first Chelsea goal was for my daughter'
Match report: Chelsea 6-3 Leeds United
news.body_en: An exhilarating second-half attacking performance saw the Blues score six goals to overcome and eliminate Leeds United and book a place in the Carabao Cup fourth round. The Blues fell behind in the opening period – Tarik Muharemovic heading in for the visitors – and appeared in danger of suffering an early exit when Brenden Aaronson drove home a second immediately after the restart. Yet our response to the adversity faced was emphatic. Two goals in two minutes from Cole Palmer, the first a penalty and the second a curled finish, brought us level, and Pedro Neto then put the Blues ahead with a well-taken strike. Alonso's side didn't relent. Welbeck struck a fourth and, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin temporarily reduced the deficit, Valentin Barco's first Chelsea goal and a second from Welbeck ensured our progress at the expense of our old rivals. In his pre-match press conference, Alonso said those who hadn't played many minutes this season would be given a chance to make their mark. The Blues head coach was true to his word, as nine changes were made to the team that started at Arsenal. Mike Penders started in goal behind a back three of Josh Acheampong, Maxence Lacroix and captain Levi Colwill. Malo Gusto and Pep Chavarria occupied the wing-back roles, 16-year-old Reggie Watson made his Chelsea debut in midfield alongside Barco, and Estevao Willian, Jamie Gittens and Danny Welbeck were in attack. Given the unfamiliarity of the starting XI, the Blues unsurprisingly took some time to settle into the game. Our best effort in the opening exchanges came from Gittens, who worked goalkeeper Michael Zetterer with an effort from distance. Leeds offered little threat until the 20-minute mark – then the visitors burst into life. Their first and second attempts on goal came in quick succession, and they brought out the best of Penders. A long throw into the Blues penalty area caused panic and the ball sat up for Aaronson. He was denied at close range by a fine stop from our Belgian goalkeeper, who then reacted instinctively to push over Muharemovic's follow-up header. However, it proved only a momentary reprieve as, after one corner was cleared behind, another Leeds delivery was met by Muharemovic at the back post, and he planted his header beyond Penders to put Leeds ahead. Leeds had momentum and looked to strike again soon after the restart. Another attack into the Blues' half ended with the ball falling to Sean Longstaff, who fired over from 18 yards. Our threat was limited during the remainder of the half. There were promising moments, such as an Estevao run that almost opened up a chance for Welbeck, an effort from Gittens deflected into the side netting, and a shot from Barco that bobbled wide, but it was a challenging half for Alonso's side. That perhaps informed the Spaniard's decision at the interval, as a quadruple substitution was made. Gusto, Watson, Estevao and Gittens were replaced. Reece James, Neto, Palmer and Rogers were introduced. It got worse for the Blues before it got better, as Leeds grabbed a second goal two minutes after the restart. It was a well-worked strike, as a low cross into the box was delicately flicked on by Lukas Nmecha and Aaronson drove home his finish. Two goals behind and facing an early cup exit, the Blues' resolve would be tested in the time that remained. Our route back into the game started with a penalty. Dan James fouled the crossing Chavarria and referee Jarred Gillett pointed to the spot. Palmer stepped up and rasped a shot into the corner. The noise inside Stamford Bridge increased. So did the tempo at which Alonso's side moved the ball. And two minutes after reducing the deficit, we levelled the contest. Palmer, again. It was a simple enough goal, as Rogers steered a long throw into the path of the Blues' No.10, who expertly guided a 20-yard finish into the corner. There was no let-up – and another attack soon followed. This time, Palmer was the provider as he guided a cross into the box for the onrushing James, whose clipped finish beat Zetterer but went the wrong side of the post. The turnaround was complete, though, on the hour mark. Palmer and Rogers were involved, as the former played a pass through to the latter, who on the slide guided the ball toward Neto. The Portuguese winger ran onto and measured his shot, which clipped the far post and nestled in the net. Still, Alonso's side pushed for more. Palmer had a low drive blocked, but our fourth goal quickly arrived. Welbeck this time on the score sheet as he collected a low cross, shifted the ball onto his right foot, evaded two challenges and fired between the legs of Zetterer. The Blues had breathing space – for ten minutes, at least. That was temporarily eroded when Calvert-Lewin drove home from inside the area and left Alonso's side facing a nervy finish. Leeds sensed there was a path to parity and committed players forward. Important blocks and defensive interventions were made; Alonso's side had to work again. Yet with ten minutes remaining, another powerful Rogers run and cross created our fifth. His delivery broke kindly to Barco, who slammed home his first Chelsea goal With that, our progress was sealed, although the scoring wasn't over. In the fourth of six added minutes, another attack ended with Barco skewing a shot toward goal, which Welbeck redirected into the corner to round off the evening. The Blues are back at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon, as we take on Hull City in Premier League action. Kick-off is at 3pm (BST), and you can follow all the action on the Chelsea Official App and website. news.title: Alonso on team selection and Reggie Watson debut
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has made nine changes tonight, including handing a debut to 16-year-old Reggie Watson, and the manager has explained his thinking behind his starting XI ahead of our Carabao Cup tie against Leeds. Alonso has altered his keeper, defence, midfield and attack for the round three fixture, which arrives between league games against Arsenal and Hull. His faith in his squad depth is one of the reasons why he has no qualms in doing so. ‘We have an intense first week of the calendar, few games, and all of them they are ready,’ said Alonso. ‘We need them to feel that they are an important part of the team and that anyone can play, and they have to be ready, so it's good from the start, and as well that players from the bench they can have a good impact as well. ‘We need a top team performance today against a very intense team as Leeds as they demand a lot, and hopefully we will have a good game.’ Watson impressed in pre-season and has been given his chance tonight in the heart of midfield, becoming the fourth-youngest player in our history in the process. Alonso explained what it is about the 16-year-old that has caught his eye since he arrived at the club. ‘He's one of those players that all the coaches like: responsible, very reliable, focused on the game. You see that he has a football background from family, so it's a great day for him. ‘I mentioned in the team talk that we have all been Reggie Watson one day, and hopefully he will enjoy it. ‘My advice to him is that he deserves to be there because of what he has shown, because of his football, because of his mentality during pre-season when he did really well. ‘We want to encourage the Academy as well, that they see the players have a chance in the first team.’

news.title: Who is Chelsea midfielder Reggie Watson, the teenager who starts against Leeds?
news.body_en: Making his Chelsea debut in our Carabao Cup third-round tie against Leeds United, we profile Academy midfielder Reggie Watson. For those who tuned into our pre-season fixtures during our summer tour of Australia and Asia, Watson will not be an unknown. The teenager featured in games against Western Sydney Wanderers, Tottenham Hotspur, AC Milan and Johor Darul Ta'zim and showcased a quality and composure that belied his years. Watson, whose father Ben represented clubs such as Crystal Palace, Wigan Athletic, Watford and Nottingham Forest during his playing career, now has the opportunity to make his mark in competitive action for the Blues – and his debut comes at Stamford Bridge. And here's what you should know about our latest debutant... Watson, who featured regularly for our Under-18s last season while still a schoolboy, was born on 26 January, 2010.  He celebrated his 16th birthday earlier this year. Watson has been regularly used as a midfielder in our Academy sides and for the first team during our pre-season tour this summer. He is an intelligent and composed player in possession and an excellent set-piece taker. Watson joined the Blues from Crystal Palace during his Under-15 season. Despite being just 16 years old, Watson has featured twice for our Cobham Next Gen side this season. He scored on his debut at that level against Bournemouth, and also netted in our recent 5-4 victory over West Ham United. Watson has represented England at Under-15 and Under-16 levels. Watson has been handed the No.31 shirt for the first team this season.

news.title: WNL Cup report: Swindon Town 1-2 Chelsea Women Under-18s
news.body_en: Chelsea Women Under-18s came from behind to secure a 2-1 victory away at Swindon Town in our second Women’s National League Cup group game. The Blues, who play in the PGA Under-21 Women's League, conceded inside the opening minute but responded strongly after the break, with Stevie Sinclair (pictured top) scoring twice to complete the comeback. The result keeps Chelsea top of Group D after two WNL Cup matches. Chelsea controlled possession from the start but were caught out when a central pass into midfield was turned over. Swindon won the first contact and transitioned quickly, with a diagonal pass finding their winger inside the Chelsea back line. The ball was struck first time with power, giving the hosts the lead after just one minute. The Blues had to work hard to defend Swindon's longer balls and adjust to a difficult surface, but remained in the contest as we looked to respond. Chelsea made three changes at the interval, with Annie Boichat, Stevie Sinclair and Chelsea N'Drin introduced for Sophie Leach, Tess Finn and Carla Gardiner. The changes helped the Blues produce a positive second-half performance, and we drew level after 64 minutes. Rebekah Pierce battled for possession after Chelsea regained the ball from a throw-in in the middle third, before receiving the ball from Elise Christian. Pierce turned outside her opponent and, after the Swindon defender went to ground, her effort from the left was palmed back into the six-yard box. Sinclair had positioned herself in the right area and reacted instinctively to finish first time. Chelsea continued to push forward and completed the turnaround with 13 minutes remaining. Pierce dropped deep to combine with Gabi Storey before playing the ball forward. N'Drin had moved into the left channel and drove at her defender before cutting inside. She then produced a well-weighted pass into the path of Sinclair on the edge of the box, with the midfielder using her left foot to lift the ball over the goalkeeper and complete her brace. The result means Chelsea sit top of Group D after two Women’s National League Cup group games. The Blues have enjoyed the challenge of playing and competing against Women's National League opposition, with this victory following our opening group-stage win. After a busy period of four games in 11 days, Chelsea return to PGA Under-21 Women's League action when we travel to Brighton on Wednesday 16 September. Some of the squad will also be away with their national teams during the international period. news.title: Inside the life of Lauren James
news.body_en: Lauren James fills us in on her footballing journey and how she likes to spend her time behind the scenes. Having trained in the Chelsea Academy from Under-10 to Under-14 level, James later signed for the Blues as a professional at the start of the 2021/22 campaign. The talented forward put pen to paper on a new contract in March, keeping her with us until 2030. We sat down with LJ to delve into what makes her tick on and off the pitch. Could you start by telling us where you grew up and what it was like? I grew up in Richmond. It's cool; it's nice there. What age did you start playing football? What was the name of your first grassroots team? Epsom Eagles, it was a boys' team. How old were you when you first joined an academy? I was six when I joined the Chelsea Academy. Who's been the biggest influence on your football career to date? Emma Hayes.She's just always been there for me, and even when she's not my manager, she's just like a mentor. I think of her as family. What's been your career highlight to date? Winning the Euros with England. Who are your best friends in football? Kadeisha Buchanan. And I've really started to bond with Melvine (Malard), too. Could you name your top three favourite players of all time? I'm going to go with Pele, Diego Maradona and Romario. What do you like to do away from football? How do you switch off? Shopping, going for food. I just like to chill with good company. Are you watching any TV series currently? I don't watch telly! Instead, I sleep, talk to my friends on the phone, go for a walk... If we looked at your Spotify playlist, who's dominating your most played artists of the year? Probably Asake. I like Afrobeats. What are your top three holiday destinations, either that you’ve been to or want to visit? Turks and Caicos Islands. Dubai. I'd just say those two, because I like going to the same places! If you had guests over for dinner, what would you cook for them? Tell the fans something they might not know about you... What's the best piece of advice you've ever received? Never listen to the opinions of people you wouldn't want advice from. Finally, what does football mean to you? Everything. It's literally my life. Don't miss out on LJ's next match at Stamford Bridge when we take on Arsenal on 27 September! Get your tickets now...

news.title: Danny Welbeck exclusive in tonight's matchday programme!
news.body_en: Danny Welbeck discusses his summer move to Chelsea, his goalscoring debut and his hopes for his time at Stamford Bridge in an exclusive interview with the matchday programme for Wednesday night’s Carabao Cup third-round tie against Leeds United. The new Blues striker headed in the first goal in our 2-0 win over Luton Town in the previous round and says he’s enjoying his early days as a Chelsea player. 'It was really nice [to score],' he says. 'I mean, it makes for a good start and it’s something that I’m looking to continue to build upon. Obviously, it was my debut at Stamford Bridge for Chelsea and it’s an honourable moment for me. So to kick it off with a goal was very pleasing. 'I feel very privileged to make the switch to Chelsea. It’s such a big club. At this stage of my career, it’s massive. I’m very honoured to receive the chance to come here and to be a part of this project. It’s exciting and one where I feel we can build something special. 'A little bit of talk is about my age, but it’s just talk. I’m here to push on, to improve. I feel really good – fit, strong, and obviously last season I had my best goalscoring season. I’m ready to push on.' Welbeck became the sixth player aged 35 or over to score for Chelsea in the 21st century, and the others on that list make up our Five feature for this programme. We’ll leave you to work out who they are before you pick up your copy, but suffice to say they are all stone-cold legends of the club. Of course, with Leeds coming to town for a cup tie, we’ll be looking back at the 1970 FA Cup final replay in our Greatest Games feature, plus there’s a look at another debutant goalscorer in Legacy, as we revisit George ‘Gatling Gun’ Hilsdon’s five-goal haul on his first appearance for Chelsea 120 years ago this month. With all the latest news and views from around the club, plus the stats and info you need ahead of the game, there’s plenty to get stuck into in the matchday programme. Pick up your copy from the programme sellers around the stadium, or order online from our publications partner, Reach Sport.

news.title: Xabi Alonso on his squad management and chances for young Blues
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso says tonight’s Carabao Cup tie against Leeds United will be an opportunity for several members of his squad to make an impact after limited minutes thus far, with the Blues manager insisting that every player must be made to feel important throughout this season. The Spaniard rotated his team successfully as the Blues defeated Luton Town 2-0 in the previous round of the League Cup, with Danny Welbeck rewarding his manager by netting the opening goal on his Chelsea debut. As our Carabao Cup campaign continues with a visit from old rivals Leeds in the third round this evening, Alonso again reiterated the need to share the minutes around his squad, knowing every one of his players will have an important part to play before the season is over. ‘We want to have the squad, as I said before, with as many players as possible involved and feeling that they have an important role,’ he said. ‘For sure you have the cups and we have the Carabao Cup. For that, we did something: we shared some minutes in the first game against Luton. ‘There will be a chance as well for other players that haven't played that much [against Leeds]. We don't have Europe, so the cups are important for us.’ Alonso also suggested some of the promising young talents coming through the Chelsea Academy at Cobham could also be involved against the Whites this evening. ‘I've said from the first day that there are some very good Academy players that have been with us in pre-season, have been training with us, and some of them will be in the squad.’ However, as always it is a balancing act, between keeping everyone fresh and sharp while ensuring we remain competitive across all fronts. That was a message Alonso reinforced when he was reminded of Chelsea’s history in the League Cup, including Jose Mourinho famously using success in this competition as the springboard for further silverware during his first spell at the Bridge. ‘We haven't used it as an example, but I remember it very well because I was on the other side,’ responded Alonso, who was in his first season with Liverpool when they lost the 2005 final to Chelsea. ‘But there is a chance. Once there is a chance, you want to fight for it, knowing where we come from, where we go to, and that this is a squad, and with only 12 or 13 players there is no chance to compete in every competition. This is the dynamic that we want for the future.’

news.title: Watch Chelsea’s 2012 League Cup rout of Leeds in full!
news.body_en: CFC+ subscribers can enjoy watching back our most recent League Cup tie against Leeds in full on the Chelsea Official App and website. The Blues take on the Whites tonight at Stamford Bridge, and ahead of that third-round tie, we have delved into the archives and dug up a classic victory over our old rivals. The setting was Elland Road and the date was 19 December 2012. The Blues had only just returned from the FIFA Club World Cup in Japan, but there were no signs of jet lag as we routed the then-Championship side by a record margin. However, it was our hosts who struck first in the 37th minute on a wet and windy evening in Yorkshire. David Luiz was caught out of position, allowing Jerome Thomas to break down the left and cross for Luciano Becchio, who finished past Petr Cech to give Neil Warnock’s side a 1–0 lead at the break. The Blues hit back immediately after the restart when Juan Mata levelled the score with a low, placed shot from the edge of the penalty area. The equaliser shifted the momentum completely as we showed our Premier League class. In the 64th minute, Branislav Ivanovic rose at the near post to head home Frank Lampard’s corner, putting Rafa Benitez’s Blues ahead. Two minutes later, Victor Moses extended the lead with a powerful shot into the top corner. Substitute Eden Hazard then made an instant impact off the bench, capping off a swift counter-attack, and soon afterwards Fernando Torres completed the rout by tapping in from close range. The away supporters enjoyed a night to remember, and you can now relive the game in its entirety below, only with a CFC+ subscription.

news.title: Oscar’s greatest goals in Blue
news.body_en: Oscar spent four-and-a-half seasons at Chelsea, producing several outstanding, memorable moments and goals. Celebrate his 35th birthday by recalling them here! The attacking midfielder joined newly crowned European champions Chelsea from Internacional as a fresh-faced 20-year-old on 25 July 2012. He was something of an unknown, having only played in his homeland Brazil, before and scoring his first international goal the previous month, although he did impress at that summer’s Olympic Games in Britain. Oscar went on to score 38 goals in 203 appearances for the Blues, helping us win the UEFA Europa League in his first season in London, then both the Premier League and League Cup two years later. He also built a reputation as a scorer of great goals, winning the Chelsea Goal of the Season award on two occasions. Oscar's time in west London ended in December 2016, when he moved to China and signed with Shanghai SIPG. He spent seven years with the club before returning to his native Brazil on Christmas Day in 2024. Sadly, after he became unwell during pre-season testing with the Brazilian club last November, Oscar was treated in hospital and required surgery. Five months later, he called time on his career. Oscar hung up his boots after winning 48 caps for his country and creating lasting memories for Chelsea supporters. We reflect on a few of them below... To score twice on your full debut is something of a dream start. For one of those strikes to win Goal of the Season is bordering on ridiculous. Yet that is exactly how Oscar announced himself to the Stamford Bridge faithful back in September 2012. Found by Ashley Cole, but with his back to goal, in a split second Oscar spun away from two Juventus shirts to create space on the edge of the box, before curling a stunning strike past Gianluigi Buffon into the top corner. The goals kept coming for Oscar in his debut Champions League campaign. He gave us the lead for the second time in this end-to-end thriller, with his countryman and future Blues team-mate Willian netting twice for Shakhtar. It may not have been the winner, but it was Oscar’s goal which lives long in the memory. It was an awkward clearance by Shakhtar keeper Andrey Pyatov, but he got enough distance on it to feel safe. That was until our No11 controlled it on his chest and lobbed him from miles out with a pinpoint half-volley. Oscar would score again as we eventually triumphed 4-0 in a replay at the Bridge, but his best came in the first game of this dramatic FA Cup fourth-round tie. Bringing down the ball with an incredible touch just outside the box but facing away from goal, the Brazilian spun away from one defender, shuffled past another into the area and poked a brilliantly improvised early finish which caught the keeper off guard to find the back of the net. Oscar had already shown his prowess from set-pieces, including one very similar goal against Stoke City the previous season, but this was arguably the pick of his free-kicks, arriving just six minutes in as we made it seven wins from eight Premier League matches. From the moment Willian was brought down on the right, Oscar knew what he was going to do, going against convention from that position by curling an effort over the wall and into the top-left corner, wrong-footing the keeper. He then combined brilliantly with Cesc Fabregas for the Spaniard to net the winning goal. This hard-fought win over stubborn opposition sent us four points clear at the top of the table on our way to claiming the Premier League title under Jose Mourinho. It was Oscar who opened the scoring with the second of his Goal of the Season winners. He was found at a difficult angle by Fabregas, but the way he curled inside the far post with a first-time effort using the outside of his boot was simply sublime.

news.title: Alonso highlights Estevao’s important role and positive mentality
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso says Estevao Willian will play an important role for the Blues throughout this season and has praised the Brazilian's attitude and mentality ahead of Leeds United's visit to Stamford Bridge in the Carabao Cup. The 19-year-old has had to remain patient in the early weeks of the new season. He has yet to start a Premier League game but was included in the side in our last Carabao Cup tie against Luton Town and produced an impressive performance. There have also been notable cameos off the substitutes' bench, the most recent coming against Arsenal on Sunday. Estevao was a whisker away from earning us a point at the Emirates Stadium, forcing goalkeeper David Raya into an excellent reaction stop late in the contest. Our Brazil international could get another chance to make his mark tonight at Stamford Bridge, and Alonso has emphasised the qualities, both on and off the pitch, that make Estevao a special talent. ‘Este is ready and is training well,’ said Alonso. ‘The other day [against Arsenal] he had a very good impact and he had a great chance. He is fully involved and has a good attitude every day. ‘I count on Este 100 per cent, because of his potential and the fact that he’s so young, he is in that process of adapting and learning quickly. ‘The season is going to be long, and players that have the desire and hunger to prove and show every day they are up for the challenge is what we want – and what we want to create here in the building. ‘Este is part of it. He has a very good attitude and mentality to prepare for every game and be ready for the team.’ Alonso was also asked where he sees Estevao fitting into our line-up and whether he could be an option to slot in at wing-back when we use that shape, as Pedro Neto and other Chelsea wingers have done under the Spaniard. ‘Whether you want to call it a back three or a back four, I know what his best position is,’ Xabi added. ‘He is more like a winger, or winger coming inside from that wide role. ‘He hasn’t played that much as a wing-back, having to track back that much. If we want to see the best of Este, he plays in that winger role.’

news.title: Chelsea vs Leeds: All you need to know
news.body_en: Welcome back to football’s house of fun, Stamford Bridge. Club historian Rick Glanvill and club statistician Paul Dutton look ahead to Chelsea hosting bitter rivals Leeds United in an 8pm kick-off in round three of the Carabao Cup. Wednesday’s game is a floodlit reprise of last season’s FA Cup semi-final at Wembley, that the Blues won more comfortably than the 1-0 scoreline suggests. In fact, Chelsea have a perfect ten out of ten record in progressing from domestic cup ties against the Yorkshiremen, three of them in the League Cup. We are also unbeaten in nine home games against the Whites across all competitions, winning seven. Last season’s Premier League clash in London ended 2-2, though. Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer (from the spot) established a two-goal lead before Lukas Nmecha and Noah Okafor claimed a share of the points for Leeds, for the first time since November 2000. The Peacocks reached this round of the Carabao Cup by winning 2-0 with virtually a full-strength line-up at Nottingham Forest. The world champions saw off League One visitors Luton Town 2-0, with debutant Danny Welbeck opening the scoring. This is a competition Chelsea last won in 2015. We remain the trophy’s first and most recent winners from the capital. All round two games are broadcast live on Sky Sports platforms and this one is on Sky Sports channels 401 and 402, plus their app. Xabi Alonso confirmed that Levi Colwill is available to feature in our Carabao Cup tie against Leeds United, but that this game comes too soon for Moises Caicedo, Marco Palestra, Emmanuel Emegha or Jordan Henderson to be involved, although he did reveal that Caicedo is back in training following his calf injury. 'Not yet, they are still not ready to go, and it's not the moment to take an early risk,' our manager explained in his pre-match press conference on Tuesday. 'So we go game by game with them, but it’s too early. 'It's especially [frustrating] for [Palestra]. He came with huge energy, huge desire to enjoy his game in the Premier League. He had a very good pre-season and a few days before the first game against Fulham, he picked up an injury. 'It’s part of the life of a football player to come back from injury and we will need him for sure. He has great potential and will add a lot of good qualities we need in the team.' Last season’s FA Cup semi-final against Leeds – a straightforward 1-0 win to Chelsea – added the latest chapter to this storied rivalry, which originated in the 1960s. As post-war England finally embraced the future, Chelsea against Leeds came to embody the conflict between haves and have-nots, tradition and modernity, north versus south. The fevered football rivalry reached its zenith in the tempestuous 1970 FA Cup final, which the Blues won 2-1 after a replay. What is less discussed is the fact that the Londoners clashed with the Yorkshiremen six times that season. Both league meetings ended in victory for the Peacocks, but two others came in round three of the League Cup. Alan Birchenall’s opener in a violent 1-1 encounter at Elland Road earned Dave Sexton’s team a replay at Stamford Bridge. The hosts won 2-0 thanks to Charlie Cooke and another from the Birch. ‘When Leeds win it is a matter of statistics, when they are beaten it is news, and when Chelsea do it to them it is good news for for all those who live in the purlieus of the King’s Road,’ wrote Geoffrey Green. That was the first occasion the two were drawn together in this competition and it was as if the footballing gods feared further retribution that a further 32 years elapsed before a repeat. High-flying United were above Claudio Ranieri’s side at kick-off in November 2001, but Chelsea ran out easy winners, with both sets of players on their best behaviour. Eidur Gudjohnsen’s ice-cold finishing brought a 2-0 win for the under-pressure Italian. Our most recent League Cup encounter was a quarter-final in Yorkshire just before Christmas 2012. By now Leeds were nine years into their tour of the Football League pyramid and the Blues took out our disappointment at losing the FIFA Club World Cup final in Japan days earlier with a club-record victory over the hosts. Overcoming a hostile crowd and torrid weather, the champions of Europe smashed Neil Warnock’s men 5-1 with five different scorers – Juan Mata, Branislav Ivanovic, Victor Moses, Eden Hazard and Fernando Torres. This is the third time in four seasons that Chelsea and Leeds have been drawn together in a cup competition. Chelsea (four) and Brighton & Hove Albion (three) are the only Premier League sides with more goals scored from set-plays than Leeds (two) this season. Only Hull (132) have played fewer successful final-third passes in the current Premier League campaign than Leeds (140). Chelsea are London’s most successful club in this competition, winning it five times, including the capital’s first and most recent successes. Our ten League Cup final appearances is bettered only by Liverpool (15). The Blues’ record victory on any front against Leeds at Elland Road was 5-1 in this competition in December 2012. On 9 September 1905, at Blackpool, John Tait Robertson scored newly-formed Chelsea’s first-ever goal. Goal-line technology and VAR will not be in operation until the semi-finals, unless all host stadiums in the round are suitably equipped. Nine substitutes can be named and five used in the game (plus a concussion replacement if required). Yellow cards and suspensions apply only to this competition. Red card bans are served across all domestic fronts. Each tie is decided on the night and extra-time is not used to decide ties until the second leg of the semi-finals. In the event of scores being level after second-half stoppage time, the outcome will be decided by a penalty shoot-out. The winners of the Carabao Cup final, played at Wembley Stadium on 21 March 2027, gain entry to next season’s UEFA Conference League play-offs.

news.title: Classic Match: Leeds Utd 1-5 Chelsea
A mutual feud forged in fire 🔥
Alonso on Henderson influence and Caicedo latest
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has explained how Jordan Henderson has already had a positive impact on the Chelsea squad as he works towards making his Blues debut, as well as providing an update on Moises Caicedo’s return from injury. Henderson joined Chelsea over the summer, bringing with him a wealth of experience and the ability to stamp his authority on games from the midfield. He is yet to feature as he recovers from an arm injury suffered while on international duty with England at this summer’s FIFA World Cup, and tomorrow’s Carabao Cup third-round tie against Leeds United will come too early for the 36-year-old to make his debut. With Henderson obviously keen to get back to full fitness and out on the pitch with his new team-mates, Alonso was asked if the midfielder has been passing his experience on to his fellow Blues in recent weeks, or if he has been fully focused on his own recovery. ‘Both! For sure he's been very close to the team,’ responded our Spanish manager. ‘Even being injured, he's been travelling with us. I know that he likes and he needs to have this connection with the team, to have this impact off the pitch, on the pitch as well. ‘In training he's doing very well, but still it's frustrating for him that even being the arm, that it's taking that long, but I think that he's in the last stage of his recovery.’ Alonso was also asked about Caicedo’s recovery from injury, having earlier confirmed that, like Henderson, the Ecuadorian midfielder will not feature at Stamford Bridge on Wednesday evening. After Caicedo's aborted comeback off the bench against Brighton & Hove Albion just over a week ago, Alonso is determined to take his time to minimise the chances of a recurrence of the injury. ‘He is training,’ revealed Xabi. ‘He has in his calf a little issue. ‘It is the same as he had before Brighton and I wanted to have Moi, and probably it was my mistake to push him too early. So that's why I'm cautious now not to make the same mistake.’

news.title: Internationals: Academy stars help England Women's Under-20s to World Cup win
news.body_en: Three Chelsea Academy graduates started as England Women Under-20s recorded a 5-1 victory over Tanzania at the Under-20 World Cup in Poland on Tuesday evening. Following a 1-1 draw with Canada in their opening match of the tournament, England Under-20s head coach Lydia Bedford selected Chelsea's Katie Cox, Vera Jones and Chloe Sarwie to start against Tanzania, with Lola Brown named among the substitutes. The young Lionesses produced a dominant display, with Aston Villa's Rachel Maltby scoring a first-half hat-trick that included two penalties and Ipswich Town's Princess Ademiluyi also on target before the break. Brown was introduced at half-time and Jessie Gale, currently on loan at Newcastle United from Arsenal, added a fifth for England in the second period. Despite a string of good saves from Cox, there would be no clean sheet as Tanzania's Jamila Mnunduka grabbed a consolation goal. England currently sit in second place in Group B and will face Brazil on Friday 11 September at 2pm.

news.title: Training gallery: Up for the cup!
Alonso: We must be ready to compete in two ways
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso expects to face an ‘intense’ Leeds United in our Carabao Cup tie at Stamford Bridge on Wednesday and has urged his players to rise to the challenge by showcasing their mentality. Our visitors from Yorkshire have proved to be challenging opposition in the final months of last season – and the first of this. They have lost just two of their past 16 games in all competitions, with one of those defeats coming against the Blues in April’s FA Cup semi-final. Alonso knows what to expect from Daniel Farke’s disciplined, dogged outfit at Stamford Bridge tomorrow, and hopes the contest will provide another opportunity for his squad to learn and improve different aspects of their game while finding a way to win the tie. ‘We are expecting a very intense game, a very tough game, with many situations of duels, but we need to try to cope with that and find solutions,’ Alonso said. ‘The adaptation to the tempo of these games is very important for some players. Some players have already done it and the approach and profile of the squad we want, and the team we want, needs to cope with that as well. ‘We need everyone involved,' added Alonso. 'The more people you have involved in the team, and the more players feel part of playing minutes, the better it is for the level. So far, the dynamic is very, very good. ‘We want to compete as it’s the best way to win games. You need to adapt to compete and it comes in two ways: in the football way and in the spirit and mentality. In everything, we can get better.’ With seven goals conceded in our three Premier League games to date, Alonso knows one area that needs improvement is our defensive work. The fact we emerged victorious from two of those matches is a source of comfort, however, and overall Alonso feels it has been a positive start to the new campaign. ‘We know that it’s going to be a long process, but you need to be assessing how things are going, and so far we can be happy,’ he said. ‘But we need to be self-demanding as well because we can do better. We can’t afford so much time to improve because we want to have clean sheets as soon as possible. That is going to be a focus in each game, but knowing that the competition is hard. ‘They (clean sheets) will come; I am 100 per cent sure they will come. We need to work, to improve the areas we can do better, and the other areas we are doing well, we need to emphasise those parts. ‘I am learning myself – from the players, from the team, from the opponents, from the Premier League – it’s part of our development, and it’s not close to the final product of this Chelsea. We have taken steps, but there are still a lot of steps to be taken.’

news.title: Aggie Beever-Jones on her 'full-circle' 100 appearances for Chelsea
news.body_en: Chelsea Academy graduate Aggie Beever-Jones made her 100th senior appearance for the club against Aston Villa at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, and when we sat down with her afterwards, we reminded her that she also made her first senior Blues appearance against the same opponent. Beever-Jones' Blues debut arrived when she was brought on as an 84th-minute substitute in a 4-0 win over the Villans back in January 2021. The striker had not already made the connection between the two landmark events, but was delighted to realise the synchronicity that now exists in her career. 'It's crazy,' Beever-Jones said. 'If you'd said that when I was in the Academy, I wouldn't have believed it. It’s a very surreal moment, and something I'm really proud of. Now I want to make many more appearances, to keep enjoying playing for the club and doing what I can. 'It’s a full-circle moment, I think, especially knowing my first and 100th were against Villa.' And while she was disappointed to only come away with a draw against Villa, Beever-Jones paid tribute to the supporters, who created a great atmosphere at the Bridge. 'The fans were brilliant on Saturday. It’s very special for Stamford Bridge to be our new home, because it's always felt like home, but for it to be official now is really exciting. 'It was really annoying about the result because I think we actually had a good game. We needed to be more clinical, but we felt the fans behind us right until the end, and it was just a shame we couldn't get it over the line. Overall, it’s really nice to be able to make Stamford Bridge our home and our fortress now, and we need to make it a place where teams are scared to come and play us.' To celebrate Aggie's milestone, we asked her to pick out her top five moments from 100 Chelsea appearances... 'I think Sio (Sjoeke Nusken) scored a hat-trick. I remember she squared it to me instead of trying to get a fourth, and I thought it was quite selfless of her. I just remember trying to get it on target, and I remember the keeper was going the other way, so I knew I had to place it back where she was coming from. 'It was such a euphoric feeling, having wanted to score for Chelsea through every moment of my childhood and then being able to do it. I remember I scored against Roma in that pre-season, and it didn't technically count as my first goal. So I think I was more motivated to score. 'I'd come back into the squad from a couple of loans, and was almost laying a marker down, saying “I'm back, I’m here now.” I loved scoring on loan but I wanted to do it for Chelsea and that goal was such a nice way to kickstart my official career with the club.' 'I started in that game. I had chances in the first half, didn't score, and then I scored in the second half. I remember Emma explaining that we needed to have a high scoreline; we all knew it, and we started the game so strongly. 'After that, we didn't take our foot off the pedal, and it was a great team performance where everyone had a big role to play. We executed the game plan so well; I remember Guro (Reiten) was on fire! We all looked at each other and almost knew we were going to do it. 'It was just a matter of time and whether we could get it done in the 90 minutes, and we did. Every time we scored, someone was running to get the ball so we could score another goal. Because it was Emma's last season, we all wanted to get back into the title race for her as well as ourselves.' 'We’d won the league already, but we wanted to win it on a high. I remember it being 0-0, and I think I had a few chances, but I knew I was going to score. I just needed one more chance. Ash (Ashley Lawrence) played me the ball in behind, and the whole pre-season Niamh (Charles) had been speaking to me about near-post finishing, because you're almost not really meant to score like that. 'She was telling me: "You just need to do it." I'd scored one in training, and she was like, "Okay, you need to do it in a game now." And I remember being in on goal, and I thought, I'm going to hit it. I hit it well, and I celebrated with the fans in the sunshine. It felt like the perfect day, because afterwards we could lift the trophy at Stamford Bridge. 'It was such a great occasion for everyone and a really nice way to end the season on a high. Overall, I have so much passion for the club, and I think being at Chelsea, we're so used to being at the top. I sometimes look back at that moment and realise it's been harder for us since. We know we need to improve and get better because the competition is getting harder.' 'My favourite goal from those four? It was a great way to start the season against Man City, but I think the free-kick against West Hamwas such a highlight, purely because I've not scored a goal like that in my career before. 'When you're in that flow state, it's almost like everything just kind of falls into place nicely, and it was a good feeling. If I had to choose, I'd say the free-kick against West Ham.' 'It wasn't the prettiest goal I've scored! It came after the start of the season with those four goals and then suffering those injuries. For me, it was really tough to pick back up on the form I was in. 'And then that was kind of a nice way to think, "Oh, I'm back again now and feel good." It’s always nice to score in a final, and even though it was the only trophy we won, it was still a trophy.'

news.title: Xabi Alonso on his early impressions of ‘competitor’ Valentin Barco
news.body_en: Our Carabao Cup second-round tie against Luton Town last month gave Blues fans their first sighting of Valentin Barco, with the Argentinean catching the eye in midfield. Ahead of our next fixture in the competition, the visit of Leeds United, Xabi Alonso has assessed the 22-year-old’s start to life at Stamford Bridge. On debut, Barco played the full 90 minutes in the middle of the park alongside Reece James. He had a hand in our second goal and created another couple of opportunities with precise passing. A few days after that Luton success, Barco made his Premier League debut as we closed out a victory over Brighton and Hove Albion. Despite only arriving at Cobham midway through August following Argentina’s run to the World Cup final, Barco has quickly impressed Alonso in their short time working together. ‘He’s a competitor,’ said our manager. ‘You see this Argentine heart; he’s a fighter. He’s very good with the ball, he is very open to adapting quickly, and he is intelligent. ‘When you have this mentality and intelligence, it’s easier to have a better impact and he’s doing that.’ Against Arsenal on Sunday, Barco was an unused substitute, with Alonso preferring to end the game with Malo Gusto and Reece James occupying the midfield roles. Yet the Blues manager insists that, as Barco continues to adapt to life at Chelsea, and with a long season ahead, there will be opportunities for our No.4 to make an impact at critical moments in matches. ‘It’s just three games in the Premier League and one game in the cup we’ve had, so it’s still early days for everything,’ said Alonso. ‘For each player and the team, many things will develop and things will happen. So, there will be chances for everyone. ‘He is patient and he is intelligent, knowing he has taken a big and important step coming from Strasbourg. Now the competition is good and he is ready for the challenge.’

news.title: Five Blues shortlisted for Ballon d’Or 2026 awards
news.body_en: The nominations for the 2026 Ballon d’Or awards have been announced and five Chelsea players are in the running to win a prize. It is the 70th anniversary of the prestigious awards, which are presented by France Football magazine and recognise achievements in the previous season. This year’s awards ceremony will be held in London in celebration of the inaugural winner Stanley Matthews. On the men’s side, our new signing Emiliano Martinez is up for Goalkeeper of the Year. Martinez won the Yashin Trophy in both 2023 and 2024, and will now be hoping to reclaim his crown following a campaign in which he helped Aston Villa win the Europa League and Argentina reach a second successive World Cup final. Four Chelsea Women players have been shortlisted across three different categories. Hannah Hampton was the inaugural winner of the Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year award last year, and she is in the running to retain that prize this time around. Hampton, who signed a new two-year deal in the summer, kept 13 clean sheets from her 25 appearances last season, including one in the Subway Women's League Cup final as we defeated Manchester United. Veerle Buurman enjoyed an outstanding debut campaign at Chelsea and the defender’s efforts have been recognised on the global stage with a nomination for the Women’s Talent of the Year award, or Kopa Trophy. Having returned from her loan at PSV Eindhoven, Buurman hit the ground running and soon established herself as an important member of Sonia Bompastor’s team, making 24 appearances during 2025/26. Her only goal of the campaign was a crucial one, as she netted a stunning 86th-minute winner in a 2-1 victory over Tottenham Hotspur that sent us to the Women’s FA Cup semi-final. Buurman was also awarded the Women’s Super League Rising Star award at the end of last season. Finally, new signings Melvine Malard and Manaka Matsukubo are both shortlisted for the Women’s Ballon d’Or. Malard joined Chelsea this summer having weighed in with 19 goal contributions for Manchester United last season, while Matsukubo was a key member of the Japan side that triumphed at the 2026 Asian Cup. She also became the youngest player to score a hat-trick in NWSL history with her three goals for North Carolina Courage against Bay FC. The Ballon d’Or awards will be announced in a ceremony at the London Palladium on Monday 26 October. Congratulations to each of our nominees!

news.title: Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea team news for Leeds visit
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has confirmed that Levi Colwill is fit and ready to feature in our Carabao Cup third-round tie against Leeds United, but four players will remain absent for the Blues. After tasting defeat for the first time this season, with Alonso's side beaten by Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday, the Blues have an immediate chance to get back to winning ways tomorrow evening against an old foe. No matter the context, games between Chelsea and Leeds always matter. And with a place in the fourth round at stake, hostilities will certainly be renewed at Stamford Bridge. On Colwill, an unused substitute against Arsenal due to a fitness issue, Alonso confirmed in his pre-match press conference that he can again call upon a defender with an understanding of the rivalry and experience in the fixture. However, there will be no Moises Caicedo or Marco Palestra, with Alonso stating neither player is ready to make their respective returns to action. ‘No, not yet,' the Blues manager replied when asked if the duo were available against Leeds. 'They are still not ready to go, and it's not the moment to take an early risk. So we go game by game with them, but it’s too early.’ Alonso, who also confirmed that summer arrivals Emmanuel Emegha and Jordan Henderson remain sidelined, admits it's been frustrating not to have been able to call upon Palestra in our opening fixtures of the campaign, especially given how the Italian international performed in pre-season 'It's especially [frustrating] for him,' the Blues boss said. 'He came with huge energy, huge desire to enjoy his game in the Premier League. He had a very good pre-season and a few days before the first game against Fulham, he picked up an injury. 'It’s part of the life of a football player to come back from injury and we will need him for sure. He has great potential and will add a lot of good qualities we need in the team.'
